# Graph Data Structures

This directory contains two different ways to represent graphs:

## `adjacency_list/`

An adjacency list representation of a graph.

- `graph_adj_list.c` - adjacency list implementation
- `graph_adj_list.h` - header file for the adjacency list graph code
- `main.c` - example or test driver
- `adj_list.png` - diagram showing the adjacency list structure
- `Makefile` - build instructions for this example

## `adjacency_matrix/`

An adjacency matrix representation of a graph.

- `graph_adj_mat.c` - adjacency matrix implementation
- `graph_adj_mat.h` - header file for the adjacency matrix graph code
- `main.c` - example or test driver
- `adj_matrix.png` - diagram showing the adjacency matrix structure
- `Makefile` - build instructions for this example

## Traversal note

I had to put the stack and queue file right here at in my graph folder, I know that it would be duplication of code,
and trust me I tried to avoid this, I'd rather spend valuable time implementing rather than try to make the code
perfectly clean from the get go. I can refactor later

- DFS would use the stack implementation
- BFS would use the queue implementation

RUNNING THE PROGRAMME:
    Please take note that to run the programme, you have to ensure that you have compiled the  queue_linked_list.c
    and stack_linked_list.c into their object files in the graphs directory
